headline: Media and entertainment see strong revenue growth while gaming shows mixed results and education invests heavily in AI.
summary: Disney and other media firms posted double‑digit revenue gains and are cutting costs. Gaming revenues are uneven, with Caesars losing money despite digital expansion. Publishing mixes AI pushes with a revenue miss at Scholastic. Education players are expanding AI initiatives and show solid revenue growth.

industries.summary: Revenue is rising across the sector, led by Disney's $25,248 m in Q2. Companies are investing in AI and cutting costs. IT spend signals are mixed, with some tightening and some expansion.

laggards.why: Revenue $1,594 m, lowest among reported firms.

themes.title: AI & tech investment
themes.detail: Disney filed an AI patent and Versant launched new digital platforms.

themes.title: Cost cutting
themes.detail: Both Disney and WBD are targeting large cost‑savings through layoffs and synergies.

industries.it_note: Some firms tighten spend while others expand, creating a varied technology buying environment.

industries.summary: Caesars posted $2,940 m revenue but a net loss, while Bally's grew 22% YoY. Digital platform rebuilds are a focus, yet margins vary.

themes.title: Digital platform rebuild
themes.detail: Caesars launched Empire Builder; Brightstar renewed lottery tech contracts.

industries.it_note: IT spend is expanding for digital casino platforms but overall outlook is uncertain.

industries.summary: Pearson shows strong revenue of $1,779 m and AI initiatives, while Scholastic missed revenue and posted a large loss. AI tools are being rolled out across products.

leaders.why: Revenue $1,779 m and positive operating margin.

laggards.why: Revenue $216.8 m and operating loss of -42.5%.
